extracted.intended_audience: State agencies, agency rulewriters, administrative law judges, agency counsel, regulated entities, and administrative law practitioners in Florida
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements and procedural standards from Florida's Administrative Procedure Act (Ch. 120) governing agency rulemaking, regulatory plans, administrative hearings, judicial review, enforcement, notices of noncompliance, and agency-specific exceptions. Useful for agency compliance, counsel advising clients, and practitioners in administrative litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract rate methodology for reimbursing DOAH services
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract rate for administrative law judge services and reimbursement of travel/video teleconferencing expenses must be based on a total-cost-recovery methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities listed (water management districts, regional planning councils, school districts, community colleges, Division of Florida Colleges, state universities, Board of Governors, State Board of Education, Florida School for the Deaf and the Blind, Commission for Independent Education) shall contract with the Division to establish the contract rate and provisions for reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of ALJs for Department of Health matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Administrative Hearings shall designate at least two administrative law judges to specifically preside over actions involving the Department of Health or boards within the Department of Health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each designated ALJ must be a member of The Florida Bar in good standing and must have legal, managerial, or clinical experience in health-care-related issues or have attained board certification in health care law from The Florida Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding funds for unpaid ALJ services to school boards
rubrics_metrics.description: If a district school board fails to make timely payment for ALJ services provided as provided annually in the General Appropriations Act, the Commissioner of Education shall withhold from any general revenue funds the district is eligible to receive an amount sufficient to pay for the ALJ services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissioner shall transfer the amount withheld to the Division of Administrative Hearings in payment of such services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings under ss. 120.569 and 120.57, no ex parte communication relative to the merits, threat, or offer of reward shall be made to the agency head after the agency head has received a recommended order, or to the presiding officer by certain persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited communicants include (a) an agency head or member of the agency or any other public employee or official engaged in prosecution or advocacy in connection with the matter or a factually related matter, and (b) a party to the proceeding, the party’s authorized representative or counsel, or any person who, directly or indirectly, would have a substantial interest in the proposed agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition on ex parte communications does not apply to advisory staff members who do not testify on behalf of the agency in the proceeding or to any rulemaking proceedings under s. 120.54.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and disclosure duties when ex parte communication received
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer involved in the decisional process who receives an ex parte communication in violation must place on the record all written communications received, all written responses, and a memorandum stating the substance of oral communications and oral responses, and shall advise all parties that such matters have been placed on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any party desiring to rebut must be allowed to do so if requested within 10 days after notice of the communication. The presiding officer may withdraw to eliminate the effect of the communication, in which case the appointing entity shall assign a successor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for prohibited ex parte communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who makes a prohibited ex parte communication, and any presiding officer who fails to place such communication in the record, is in violation of the act and may be assessed a civil penalty not to exceed $500 or be subjected to other disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of agency personnel for bias, prejudice, or interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual serving alone or with others as an agency head may be disqualified from serving in an agency proceeding for bias, prejudice, or interest when any party shows just cause by a suggestion filed within a reasonable period of time prior to the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disqualified, an appointing power may appoint a substitute; if elected, the Governor may appoint a substitute. If a quorum remains after disqualification, no substitute is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of substitute for disqualified individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agency action taken by a duly appointed substitute for a disqualified individual shall be as conclusive and effective as if action had been taken by the agency as originally constituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review of final agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: A party adversely affected by final agency action is entitled to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary, procedural, or intermediate orders are immediately reviewable if final review would not provide an adequate remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue and timing for seeking judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review must be sought in the appellate district where the agency maintains its headquarters or where a party resides, or as otherwise provided by law; proceedings are instituted by filing a notice of appeal or petition for review in accordance with the Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure within 30 days after rendition of the order being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the appeal is of an order rendered in a proceeding initiated under s. 120.56, the agency whose rule is being challenged shall transmit a copy of the notice of appeal to the committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and transfer of appellate proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When proceedings are consolidated for final hearing and parties seek review in more than one district court of appeal, the courts may transfer and consolidate the review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider in transfer include interrelationship of parties/proceedings, avoiding inconsistent results, judicial economy, and record reproduction burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay and supersedeas rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing the petition does not itself stay enforcement of the agency decision, but if the agency decision suspends or revokes a license, supersedeas shall be granted as a matter of right upon reasonable conditions unless the court determines a supersedeas would constitute a probable danger to the health, safety, or welfare of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may grant a stay on appropriate terms; petitioning the agency for a stay is not a prerequisite to petitioning the court. The court shall specify conditions of stay or supersedeas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review confined to the record
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial review of any agency action shall be confined to the record transmitted and any additions made thereto in accordance with paragraph (7)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record for judicial review shall be compiled in accordance with the Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and powers of the reviewing court's decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing court's decision may be mandatory, prohibitory, or declaratory in form, and shall provide whatever relief is appropriate irrespective of the original form of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court may order agency action required by law, order agency exercise of discretion when required, set aside agency action, remand for further proceedings, decide rights/privileges/obligations, and order ancillary relief necessary to redress effects of official action wrongfully taken or withheld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: remand if no hearing and disputed facts affect validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand to the agency for further proceedings when there has been no hearing prior to agency action and the reviewing court finds that the validity of the action depends upon disputed facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: remand if findings not supported by competent substantial evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand or set aside agency action when the agency's action depends on any finding of fact that is not supported by competent, substantial evidence in the record of a hearing conducted pursuant to ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the court shall not substitute its judgment for that of the agency as to the weight of evidence on any disputed finding of fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: remand for material procedural error or failure to follow prescribed procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand when the fairness of the proceedings or correctness of the action may have been impaired by a material error in procedure or a failure to follow prescribed procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: remand for erroneous interpretation of law
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand when the agency has erroneously interpreted a provision of law and a correct interpretation compels a particular action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground: remand for improper exercise of discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall remand when the agency's exercise of discretion was outside the range delegated by law, inconsistent with agency rule, inconsistent with officially stated agency policy or prior practice without explanation, or otherwise in violation of a constitutional or statutory provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court shall not substitute its judgment for that of the agency on an issue of discretion absent these grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmance presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the court finds a ground for setting aside, modifying, remanding, or ordering agency action under a specified provision, it shall affirm the agency’s action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on challenging an agency rule under this section
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition challenging an agency rule as an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority shall not be instituted pursuant to this section except to review an order entered pursuant to certain proceedings (s.120.56 or s.120.57(1)(e)1. or (2)(b)) or an agency’s findings prerequisite to emergency rule adoption, unless the sole issue is constitutionality and there are no disputed facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review for ALJ factual findings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an administrative law judge's final order depends on any fact found by the ALJ, the court shall not substitute its judgment for that of the ALJ as to the weight of the evidence on any disputed finding of fact, but shall set aside or remand if the final order depends on any finding not supported by competent, substantial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may seek enforcement of agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agency may seek enforcement by filing a petition for enforcement in the circuit court where the subject matter of the enforcement is located; a petition for enforcement may also be filed by any substantially interested person who is a resident of the state (in the name of the State of Florida on the relation of the petitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, no such action may be commenced prior to 60 days after the petitioner has given notice of the violation to the head of the agency concerned, the Attorney General, and any alleged violator, and not if an agency has already filed and is diligently prosecuting a petition for enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies available in enforcement petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for enforcement may request declaratory relief; temporary or permanent equitable relief; any fine, forfeiture, penalty, or other remedy provided by statute; any combination of the foregoing; or, absent other statutory authority, a fine not to exceed $1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata and collateral estoppel in enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for enforcement by a nongovernmental person shall be in the name of the State of Florida on the relation of the petitioner, and the doctrines of res judicata and collateral estoppel shall apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After judgment on a petition for enforcement, no other petition shall be filed/adjudicated against the same agency action on the same transaction unless expressly authorized on remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency intervention in enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action brought by a nongovernmental person, the agency whose action is sought to be enforced, if not a party, may intervene as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may ascertain facts and consolidate proceedings in enforcement matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If enforcement depends on facts other than those appearing in the record, the court may ascertain such facts under procedures in s.120.68(7)(a). If multiple petitions for enforcement and a petition for review involving the same agency action are pending, the court may order consolidation and transfer; each party must notify the court when aware of multiple proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contempt for willful failure to comply with court orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Should any party willfully fail to comply with an order of the court, the court shall punish that party in accordance with contempt law applicable to trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses available to respondent in enforcement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may assert as defenses the invalidity of any relevant statute, inapplicability of the administrative determination to the respondent, compliance by the respondent, the inappropriateness of the remedy sought, or any combination thereof. If the enforcement petition is filed during the time respondent could have petitioned for judicial review, the respondent may assert the invalidity of the agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency's authority to seek immediate temporary relief for imminent threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding other provisions, upon receipt of evidence an alleged violation presents an imminent and substantial threat to public health, safety, or welfare, the agency may bring suit for immediate temporary relief in an appropriate circuit court; such temporary relief shall not have res judicata or collateral estoppel effect as to further relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding costs and fees in enforcement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In any final order on a petition for enforcement the court may award to the prevailing party all or part of litigation costs and reasonable attorney's fees and expert witness fees when the court determines such an award is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy favoring notice of noncompliance for minor violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The state policy is that regulation's purpose is to protect the public by attaining compliance; fines and penalties are secondary. Agencies shall issue a notice of noncompliance as their first response to a minor violation where it is reasonable to assume the violator was unaware or unclear how to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of noncompliance: content and prohibition on penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'notice of noncompliance' must identify the specific rule being violated, provide information on how to comply with the rule, and specify a reasonable time for compliance. It may not be accompanied by a fine or other disciplinary penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'rule' for this purpose is agency action that regulates a business/occupation/profession or a person operating such that noncompliance may result in disciplinary penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation process for minor violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall review all rules and designate those for which violation would be a minor violation and for which a notice of noncompliance must be the first enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A violation is 'minor' if it does not result in economic or physical harm to a person, does not adversely affect public health/safety/welfare, and does not create a significant threat of such harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and publication for agency minor-violation certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than June 30, 2017, and thereafter within 3 months after request of the rules ombudsman, each agency shall review and certify to legislative leaders and the rules ombudsman those rules designated as minor-violation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning July 1, 2017, agencies must publish all designated rules (complete list on website or incorporation in disciplinary guidelines), ensure investigative/enforcement personnel are knowledgeable, and certify on rule filings whether any part is designated minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to notice-of-noncompliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section does not apply to the Department of Corrections; educational units; regulation of law enforcement personnel; or regulation of teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation pursuant to this section is not subject to challenge under this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual regulatory plan requirement and due date
rubrics_metrics.description: By October 1 of each year, each agency shall prepare and publish a regulatory plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must include specified listings and certifications about laws, rulemaking needs, and planned rule reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory plan requirement: listing laws affecting agency and rulemaking status
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must list each law enacted or amended in the prior 12 months that creates or modifies agency duties/authority. For each listed law the plan must state whether the agency must adopt rules to implement the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rulemaking is necessary, the plan must state whether a notice of rule development was published (citation) and the date the agency expects to publish the notice of proposed rule. If rulemaking is not necessary, provide a concise written explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory plan: listing laws agency expects to implement by rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must list each law not otherwise listed which the agency expects to implement by rulemaking before the following July 1 (except emergency rulemaking) and state whether the rulemaking is intended to simplify, clarify, increase efficiency, improve coordination, reduce regulatory costs, or delete obsolete/unnecessary/redundant rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory plan: schedule for rule reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must include a list of existing rules scheduled for review pursuant to s. 120.5435, a 5-year schedule for review of all existing rules as of July 1, 2025, and a yearly schedule for rules to review each year during the 5-year period; the agency may amend the schedule if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agency has untimely rule reviews from prior years, it must identify and list such rules as untimely and notify the committee, or explain why review is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing performance tracking to include in regulatory plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning Oct 1, 2025, agencies issuing licenses under s.120.60 shall track compliance with licensing timeframes and by Oct 1, 2026 must include in the regulatory plan for the prior fiscal year specified licensing information categorized by type of license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required metrics include: (a) number of license applications submitted; (b) number requiring one or more requests for additional information; (c) number for which applicant was nonresponsive to requests; (d) number not completed by applicant; (e) number for which agency requested applicant extension for agency actions and number where extension requested by applicant or required by state agency/judicial branch; (f) number not approved or denied within statutory timeframe; (g) average and median days to approve/deny after receipt of a completed application; (h) number of applications for which final agency action was appealed and number of informal/formal hearings requested; (i) number of employees dedicated to processing license applications, if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, delivery, and maintenance of regulatory plan
rubrics_metrics.description: By October 1 each year, each agency shall publish its regulatory plan on its website (clear hyperlink on primary homepage) or another state website, electronically deliver the required certification to the committee, and publish a notice in the Florida Administrative Register identifying plan publication with hyperlink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A regulatory plan shall be maintained at an active website for 10 years after initial publication. Boards receiving administrative support may coordinate inclusion with the supporting department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department review and certification of board regulatory plans
rubrics_metrics.description: By October 15 each year, the Department of Business and Professional Regulation shall file certifications that it has reviewed each board's/commission's regulatory plan for boards it supports; the Department of Health shall file similar certifications for boards it supports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification may relate to more than one board or commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting and supplementing the regulatory plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A published regulatory plan may be corrected at any time to name an affected rulemaking proceeding; corrections are deemed corrected as of the October 1 due date and a notice of correction must be published in the Florida Administrative Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After publication, the agency must supplement the plan within 30 days after a bill becomes law if it substantively modifies the agency's duties (unless the law affects most agencies as identified by the Governor/AG). Supplements require publication and certain rule-development notices within specified timeframes (notice of rule development within 30 days, notice of proposed rule within 180 days), otherwise the law must be listed in next annual plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to comply with plan publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency fails to comply with publication/delivery requirements within 15 days after written demand from the committee or chair of a legislative committee, the agency shall deliver a written explanation of reasons for noncompliance to the committee, legislative leaders, and the requesting committee chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from regulatory plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This section (regulatory plan requirements) does not apply to educational units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Administrative Hearings as a party: hearing officer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Division of Administrative Hearings is a party, a hearing may not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the division; an attorney assigned by the Administration Commission shall be the hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workers' compensation judges excluded from being 'agency' under chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding s.120.52(1), a judge of compensation claims adjudicating matters under chapter 440 is not an agency or part of an agency for purposes of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing orders under certain chapters are not rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing orders under chapter 527, 573, or 601 are not rules for purposes of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, hearings held by the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services pursuant to chapter 601 need not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Financial Regulation special notice and hearing timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For license/renewal/merger proceedings under title XXXVIII, the Office of Financial Regulation must publish notice in the Florida Administrative Register within 21 days after receipt; any person may request a hearing within 21 days after publication (failure to request constitutes waiver), but OFR or an applicant may request a hearing at any time prior to final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hearing is requested, the applicant/licensee must publish notice of the hearing in a newspaper of general circulation at its own cost; the Financial Services Commission may by rule specify format/size of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFR licensing decision timelines and deemed approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, an application for certain financial institution licenses must be approved or denied within 180 days after receipt of the original application or receipt of timely requested additional information or correction; if not approved/denied within 180 days (or within 30 days after conclusion of a public hearing), it shall be deemed approved subject to completion of statutory conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special timeline for foreign national ownership/control matters: such applications must be approved or denied within 1 year after receipt of original application or requested information, or within 30 days after conclusion of public hearing, whichever is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ report and exceptions in OFR-referred proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application pursuant to title XXXVIII is referred to the division for hearing, the ALJ shall complete and submit a written report of findings of fact and rulings on evidentiary matters; the agency shall allow each party at least 10 days to submit written exceptions to the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: DBPR hearings: prohibition on Secretary/board members presiding
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding s.120.57(1)(a), formal hearings for matters relating to the regulation of professions may not be conducted by the Secretary of Business and Professional Regulation or a board or member of a board within the DBPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Land and Water Adjudicatory Commission ALJ assignment notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission receives a notice of appeal pursuant to s. 380.07, it shall notify the Division within 60 days after receipt of the notice if it elects to request assignment of an ALJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Law Enforcement policy/procedures not classified as rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Law enforcement policies and procedures related to specified sensitive activities are not rules under this chapter. These include collection/management/dissemination of active criminal intelligence and investigative information; management of criminal investigations; undercover investigations and selection/assignment/fictitious identity of undercover personnel; recruitment/management/identity/remuneration of confidential informants; surveillance techniques including electronic surveillance; safety and release of hostages; provision of security/protection to public figures; and protection of witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Children and Families hearings exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings conducted within the Department of Children and Families in execution of social and economic programs administered by the former Division of Family Services need not be conducted by an ALJ assigned by the division.
